pairs.difference: A: the ball sits upright and centered on rippled sand, with a calm band of dunes above it. Its margin of 0.121 is slightly loose. B: the ball is pushed close to the camera and tilted, and it takes up 0.493 of the card, above the real range. Its large soft cast shadow and the dimpled sand fill what little space remains, so there is less breathing room around the hero. The signal is weak because both cards read instantly as a beach ball.
pairs.fix: Draw the beach ball smaller, centered, with clear sand and sky space on all sides and a short shadow on one side.

pairs.difference: A: the target on the left and the bear on the right sit side by side on a shelf under a light arch, so they form one balanced group. B: the target is centered and the bear is jammed against the right edge (margin 0.019), overlapping the booth post. Heavy posts and a dark band along the bottom add weight, and the bear crowds the target for attention.
pairs.fix: Move the bear fully inside the booth with a clear gap from the right edge, and let the shelf run off both sides with no dark band below it.

pairs.difference: A: the unit sits left of center, slightly smaller, with airflow trailing to the lower left. B: the unit is larger and shifted right, close to the edge (margin 0.033), with a ceiling strip across the top. Both have the same wide, low subject and a plain striped wall, and both box heights fall below the real range. Nothing on this vector separates them.

A: the chest is large and turned, with the lid swinging across the upper right and bubbles overlapping it, so it fills the card with energy (margin 0.063). B: the chest is smaller, squarer to the viewer and fully isolated in the middle (margin 0.126, above the real range), with shell and coins set out as tidy props on both sides. This matches the lessons' centered, complete generated layout.
pairs.fix: Draw the chest bigger and turned at a stronger angle, with the lid nearly reaching the card edge and fewer small props beside it.

pairs.difference: A: the cap fills the width at low eye level against a simple plank wall, and its anchor badge is the first read. B: the cap is smaller (area 0.251, height 0.492) and seen from above in a room corner. The corner post, skirting boards and steep diagonal floorboards compete with it, and a diagonal shadow cuts across the upper right.
pairs.fix: Draw the cap larger from a low front angle against a plain flat wooden wall, with the floor as one calm band and no room corner.

pairs.difference: A: the small crown pattern on the wall is quiet and echoes the crowns on the booth, so the booth stays alone as the focus, and a long shadow grounds it. B: oversized tilted suitcase shapes on the wall are almost as large as the booth's upper body, are unrelated to it, and pull the eye away from the hero at thumbnail size.
pairs.fix: Replace the big suitcases with a small, quiet repeat pattern on the wall that stays far behind the phone booth.

pairs.difference: A: two gloves sit diagonally with their black cuffs visible and a gap between them, so at thumbnail size they read as a clean pair, with margins inside the real range. B: the gloves pile into one red mass spanning 0.951 of the width (above the real range), nearly touching both sides (margin 0.021). The cuffs are mostly hidden, so the pair is slower to read.
pairs.fix: Draw two separate gloves side by side at a slight angle with a visible gap, both black cuffs showing, and clear space from the left and right edges.

pairs.difference: A: the fins are thin and small on the card (measured 0.516 by 0.531, below the real range), and the dark blades sink into the purple rings. B: the two fins are broad and bold, in range at 0.874 by 0.679, with an orange rim that lifts them off the ground, and they read at once. The evidence is weak because the mask may have caught only part of A.
pairs.fix: Draw the fins much bigger on the card, filling it corner to corner, with broad yellow blades that stand out clearly from the purple.

pairs.difference: A: a whole pier sits low against sea and sky with a beach foreground. It reads instantly as a dock, though the hero is modest (area 0.26). B: a tight, high-angle view of two posts and a big life ring, with the deck running off the right edge. The first read is the ring and rope rather than a dock, and the shoreline in the top corner adds a second area of interest.
pairs.fix: Pull the camera back to show the whole small pier from the front at low eye level, with the life ring as a small accent on one post.

pairs.difference: A: a thick curved trunk and heavy fronds make a bold single shape, large coconuts mark the center, and the quiet sand holds a soft shadow. B: the tree is thinner, with a spidery spread of fronds. The strong spiral behind the crown and two bright white rocks at the bottom compete with it, so the hero's shape is weaker at thumbnail size.
pairs.fix: Draw a thicker trunk and fuller rounded fronds, soften the background swirl, and make the rocks small and sand-colored.

pairs.difference: A: the locker is turned to the left with its door open on the right, and a soft wall shadow and angled baseboard give it a dynamic stance. B: it stands more frontal and upright, with a flat wall and a level baseboard, and the contents are stacked neatly in the center. It is the more static, symmetrical layout seen on generated lesson cards. The two scales are almost identical, so the signal is weak.
pairs.fix: Turn the locker further to a three-quarter angle, with the wall and baseboard receding in perspective.

pairs.difference: A: a clean S-curve leads the eye from the yellow platform down to the splash in the pool, and the pool corner anchors the lower left. It reads at once as a water slide. B: the slide is one bulky green loop cut across by a post, and the lower end stops short of the water. The tall, high-contrast pink waves behind it fight the hero, and the card feels crowded and less clear at thumbnail size.
pairs.fix: Draw a slim slide in an open S-shape ending in a splash in the pool, and make the background waves wide, soft and low-contrast.

pairs.difference: A: the player is small and sits upper left, with earbuds trailing lower right, so the card has a diagonal balance but a weak first read (no icon, area 0.219). B: the player is large and centered with a clear play symbol, and it reads faster, with cables to the right. Each is in range and the differences run both ways, so there is no reason to choose on this vector.

A: the envelope is tilted and the photos fan out wide to both sides, giving a lively diagonal silhouette, like the tilted real ticket card. B: the envelope is nearly level and centered, with the photos bunched to one side, inside a neat rounded block (margin 0.105). It is a calmer, more static placement.
pairs.fix: Tilt the envelope clearly to one side and fan the photos out wider, with their corners reaching toward the card edges.

pairs.difference: A: the plate is seen from near table level against a striped wall, with the watermelon rising as a clear peak and the wall and table as simple bands. B: the plate is seen from above on diagonal wood planks, tilted across the card. The strong plank lines compete with it, and the fruit forms a busy heap with no clear single peak.
pairs.fix: Lower the camera to near table level, stand the watermelon slice tall at the back of the plate, and put a plain flat wall behind it.

pairs.difference: A: the door is cropped close and bleeds off the top and bottom, and ivy runs off the corners. The wreath is the first read, like the real cropped lighthouse in the lessons. The low 0.081 area and 0.279 margin look like the mask catching only the wreath. B: the whole arched door is shown symmetrically and centered, with step, wall and ivy all fully contained, the safe complete layout of the generated lesson cards.
pairs.fix: Crop in on the door so it runs off the top and bottom of the card, and make the wreath large in the center.

pattern: Generated cards tend to default to a safe, complete layout. The whole object is kept inside the card, placed upright or nearly frontal, and centered, with tidy props set around it. Real cards more often tilt the hero, turn it at a stronger angle, or crop it with an edge. Generated cards also let the setting compete: large wall motifs, strong swirls or waves, diagonal planks and bright rocks. When they push scale, the hero crowds an edge or merges into one mass, as with the gloves and the bear. This is a weak signal in many pairs: measured values mostly overlap the real ranges, and some are unreliable where the mask caught only part of the subject.
